text:
Stian Solberg will remember Friday for the right reasons and the wrong ones. The 2024 first-round pick scored his first NHL goal, then his second 76 seconds later, and the Ducks led the Kings 2-0 in the first period. Los Angeles then scored five of the next six and won 5-3.

Solberg's first came on a snap shot at 14:20 off Mikael Granlund and Alex Killorn. His second, at 15:36, was a 1% chance by our numbers, the least likely goal of the night. Anaheim was playing without Leo Carlsson, placed on injured reserve this week according to Daily Faceoff, and for a period it didn't seem to matter.

The second period was a shootout in all but name, 1.48 to 1.44 in expected goals (the quality of chances, added up). Mats Zuccarello scored twice in the first 5:30, on a 3% and a 6% chance, both set up by Kevin Fiala, and Adrian Kempe gave the Kings the lead at 8:49 with Artemi Panarin on the play. Beckett Sennecke, back from injury and on Anaheim's top power play, tied it with a slap shot at 12:32. Brian Dumoulin's assist on Zuccarello's first goal was the 200th point of his career, and he added another early in the third when Andre Lee tipped in the winner at 2:16. That goal swung LA's win chance from 48% to 74%. Darcy Kuemper's biggest stop came late, on a 20% look from Killorn, before Trevor Moore sealed it at 18:39.

The finishing was the story on both sides. Laurent Brossoit allowed four goals on 20 shots, about 1.9 more than those shots deserved, and Kuemper was a little below expected too. Our replays of every shot actually favored Anaheim, 56% to 44%, and the Ducks outattempted the Kings 62 to 46. The Kings won 38 of 58 faceoffs and found a way, which is what Peter Laviolette's team has done often this month. For Anaheim, a rookie defenseman's breakout night ended with a loss to its biggest rival, and with Carlsson out, nights where the chances are close and the goaltending isn't will keep costing them.
headline: Solberg's first two NHL goals not enough as Kings rally
